title: Predicting Purchase Behavior Using Long Short-Term Memory Networks and Customer Segmentation
authors: Ciric, V.; Obradovic, N.; Pavlovic, I.
tldr: Two LSTM architectures—a sequence model and an attribute-enhanced model incorporating customer age, gender, and location—predict future purchases from real e-commerce data, with the attribute-enhanced model showing statistically significant improvements for short prediction windows.
problem_and_motivation: Accurate purchase prediction is essential for optimizing inventory management and enhancing customer experience, yet existing collaborative filtering and sequence prediction methods lack granularity. Traditional methods focus on what to recommend rather than predicting precise purchase timing and quantities from sequential patterns. There is a need for models that capture fine-grained temporal dependencies while incorporating demographic attributes.
approach: Developed two LSTM-based architectures: a pure sequence model and an attribute-enhanced model incorporating customer age, gender, and location.
Trained models on real e-commerce datasets from three distinct industries.
Implemented preprocessing pipeline to extract and encode customer demographics, product features, and sequential purchase data.
Evaluated models using predictive accuracy metrics including MAE, MSE, and RMSE.
Conducted statistical significance testing using ANOVA with Tukey HSD post-hoc analysis.
Tested prediction performance across 7, 14, and 21-day prediction windows.
Compared LSTM performance against baseline logistic regression and LSTM classifiers.
findings: Attribute-enhanced LSTM outperforms the pure sequence model for short prediction windows (7-14 days) with statistical significance.
Prediction accuracy degrades for longer prediction windows (21 days) across all models.
Customer age and gender significantly influence purchase patterns and improve predictive performance.
Logistic regression outperforms LSTM classifiers on structured tabular data.
MAE values are approximately 10x lower than RMSE values, indicating sparse but extreme purchase events.
Performance varies across industries, reflecting differing consumer behavior patterns.
Location attributes do not significantly improve prediction accuracy.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes two LSTM architectures for purchase prediction that integrate both sequential transaction patterns and customer demographic attributes, demonstrating that attribute-enhanced models achieve statistically significant improvements over pure sequence models for short-term prediction windows. The work validates these findings across multiple e-commerce industries, showing that customer age and gender are significant predictors while location is not, and establishing that logistic regression outperforms LSTM classifiers on structured tabular purchase data.
directly_justifies: Attribute-enhanced LSTM significantly outperforms pure sequence models for 7-14 day prediction windows.
Customer age and gender significantly improve purchase prediction accuracy.
Prediction accuracy degrades substantially for longer prediction horizons (21 days).
Logistic regression outperforms LSTM classifiers on structured tabular data.
MAE is approximately 10x lower than RMSE indicating sparse extreme purchase events.
limits: Performance varies across industries, limiting generalizability claims.
Location attributes did not improve prediction, suggesting limited demographic feature value.
Long-term prediction (21 days) shows degraded performance across all models.
Statistical significance only established for short prediction windows.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) received high relevance as the core contribution is LSTM-based purchase prediction. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) received medium relevance for customer profiling using demographics. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) received medium relevance for reviewing recommendation approaches. Domains 1-3, 7-8, 10-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial data APIs, expense categorization, budgeting, anomaly detection, privacy, engagement, mobile design, evaluation frameworks, or synthetic data generation.

limitations: Industry-specific performance variation limits cross-domain generalizability.
Location attributes do not contribute to prediction accuracy.
Long-term prediction horizon (21 days) shows substantial performance degradation.
Statistical significance only demonstrated for short prediction windows.
